summary: The first preservation census read pin evidence from the REQUEST (source_origin.artifacts) instead of the RECEIPT (hashes.artifacts) and reported 59 fossils with unpinned artifacts when the true count was 18. This record preserves the erroneous result rather than deleting it.

failure.when: batch 09, 2026-09-13, first run of preservation_census over n=109
failure.mechanism: acquire() writes the resolved pin to both source_origin and hashes.artifacts. Every batch script's main() then rebuilds the record from a literal skeleton, carrying forward only run_classification/test_classification/receipts/hashes/acquisition_date/observability/nyx_handoff. source_origin is NOT carried forward, so re-running a batch script overwrites it and destroys the request-side pin. The census then read the destroyed half.
failure.how_caught: The 59 figure was implausible against the knowledge that acquire() records sha256 for every url artifact, so the two fields were compared directly on three specimens (bdwgc-8.2.6, avida, buddy-bdd). All three carried the pin in hashes.artifacts and lacked it in source_origin.
failure.what_it_would_have_cost: Reporting 54% of the vault as unpinned would have mis-ranked the entire preservation-debt queue and hidden the 2 genuinely incomplete bodies among 59 false positives.

repair_batch_10.reader: unchanged -- batch 09 already corrected it to consult the receipt first
repair_batch_10.writer: record.merge_artifact_pins() added; all 9 batch main() blocks now call it, so rebuilding a record can no longer destroy an established pin
repair_batch_10.controls: techne/tests/test_pin_evidence.py -- C1 reproduces the 59-error with the legacy request-only predicate and shows the authoritative reader disagreeing; C2 prevents C1 passing for a reader that always says pinned; C3 reproduces the writer defect and shows the fix repairing it; C4 asserts no record in the vault asks a re-acquisition to trust a moving HEAD. Falsifiability verified by disabling the fix and observing C3 fail.

P-B.claim: the preservation census counts DO NOT MOVE (97/2/18/0 at n=117)
P-B.outcome: CONFIRMED -- identical after the change, because the reader already consulted the receipt. The defect was never about the census counts; it was about whether this exact body can be reconstructed without trusting a moving HEAD.

P-C.claim: re-running a batch script is idempotent with respect to pins
P-C.outcome: CONFIRMED by test_c4b over a 20-specimen sample

lesson: A census that reads the wrong field is not a census of the vault, it is a census of the field. The number was wrong by 3.3x while every underlying body was unchanged -- the bodies were never the thing that moved.
